newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi governor blasts tobacco deals. [corrected 23:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Mississippi governor blasts tobacco deals. [corrected 23:30 GMT]

text.p: Gov. Kirk Fordice, who has long opposed his state's lawsuit against the tobacco industry, said Thursday Mississippi's $3.36 (corrects figure from $3.6) billion settlement with cigarette makers set a dangerous precedent.

Blasting the agreement as a deal "about big bucks and big publicity," the staunch Republican conservative said the state agreement, like its national counterpart, was sure to do little more than to enrich a small group of trial lawyers.
"This is a dangerous precedent: a sin tax levied by the way of litigation, not legislation," Fordice said in a statement.

"If this new tax on smokers is in fact going to be assessed and billions collected, I would have preferred that it had been done by the state legislatures or Congress, in keeping with the democratic traditions of our country."

The state settlement ended the threat of a lawsuit against the tobacco industry that was to go to trial next Wednesday. The deal dwarfed the $940 million sought by the state as compensation for tax dollars spent treating Medicaid recipients for smoking-related illnesses.
Mississippi was the first state to sue the industry in 1994 and on Thursday also became the first to announce an individual settlement.

Fordice had sued to block Attorney General Mike Moore, a Democrat, from pressing ahead with his suit against the industry. But the Mississippi Supreme Court threw out the governor's challenge in March.

The Mississippi agreement could be supplanted by the $368.5 billion national settlement between cigarette makers and 40 state attorneys general, including Moore, who have all filed suits against the industry. The larger accord needs approval in Congress and already has come under fire from opponents.

"The tobacco companies seem to have bought their peace and the trial lawyers will probably cash in beyond their wildest dreams," Fordice said. "When confronted with these two extremes, I don't really see any heroes or much to applaud."
